searchText: I often make requests for EF devops to block spam accounts from ethereum github repos. They're very quick about it. If you see something in an ethereum repo, feel free to message me with their account and I'll forward it to devops. Maybe a new "github-spam-reports" channel would be useful. just fyi raised https://github.com/eth-clients/holesky/pull/120 and https://github.com/eth-clients/sepolia/pull/99 which should cover off on the fields other than the fork epoch for electra for sepolia and holesky <@199561711278227457> sepolia would require 97,98,99 to be electra ready IMO holesky would need 118,119,120 to be electra ready. Theres one of those on each dependent on the final testnet dates could you bring this up at ACD? Or add it to the issue so we can discuss it? yep ok, i'll tyr to be awake but its super late, i'll add it to the pm I also had questions from a staking group about whether there was likely to be documentation on how the parital withdrawals contract etc works so they can make use of it, if anyone knows where that may be? The docs are kind of in the EIP I have added a little Solidity snippet in the EIP that shows how to use it: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7002#fee-overpayment But please note that this should probably be extended in prod code to guard against high fees The audit of the system contract noted that the fee updates only once per block, which may lead to some pretty radical fee swings I actually still think this issue is a serious one Talked about this with <@543900561460822016> a while ago, and he said that we could change the contract to recompute the fee after adding each request, but it would cost more gas. the 'excess' is only computed once per block this is true, a gas limit of a block would be the limitation on how much the fee can go up after processing a block i think this is fine as long as we can keep up to a few thousands requests in the queue, it doesn't sound like a good UX though, but i don't know if updating fee per each transaction can improve it much considering the case with a ton of requests in one transaction <@425572898787426305> this is amazing https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4112, is it worth checking if this would have caught the bug we had in Lodestar before merging? yeah, it would be great to check if possible new_validator_deposit_with_multiple_epoch_transitions

excerpts.author: jtraglia
excerpts.content: I often make requests for EF devops to block spam accounts from ethereum github repos. They're very quick about it. If you see something in an ethereum repo, feel free to message me with their account and I'll forward it to devops. Maybe a new "github-spam-reports" channel would be useful.

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content:
just fyi raised https://github.com/eth-clients/holesky/pull/120 and https://github.com/eth-clients/sepolia/pull/99 which should cover off on the fields other than the fork epoch for electra for sepolia and holesky <@199561711278227457> 
sepolia would require 97,98,99 to be electra ready IMO
holesky would need 118,119,120 to be electra ready.
Theres one of those on each dependent on the final testnet dates

excerpts.author: parithosh
excerpts.content: could you bring this up at ACD? Or add it to the issue so we can discuss it?

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: yep ok, i'll tyr to be awake but its super late, i'll add it to the pm

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: I also had questions from a staking group about whether there was likely to be documentation on how the parital withdrawals contract etc works so they can make use of it, if anyone knows where that may be?

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: The docs are kind of in the EIP

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: I have added a little Solidity snippet in the EIP that shows how to use it: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7002#fee-overpayment

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: But please note that this should probably be extended in prod code to guard against high fees

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: The audit of the system contract noted that the fee updates only once per block, which may lead to some pretty radical fee swings

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: I actually still think this issue is a serious one

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: Talked about this with <@543900561460822016> a while ago, and he said that we could change the contract to recompute the fee after adding each request, but it would cost more gas.

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: the 'excess' is only computed once per block

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: this is true, a gas limit of a block would be the limitation on how much the fee can go up after processing a block

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: i think this is fine as long as we can keep up to a few thousands requests in the queue, it doesn't sound like a good UX though, but i don't know if updating fee per each transaction can improve it much considering the case with a ton of requests in one transaction

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: <@425572898787426305> this is amazing https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4112, is it worth checking if this would have caught the bug we had in Lodestar before merging?

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: yeah, it would be great to check if possible
